subtopics.title: Ten Thousand Years of Slow, Two Centuries of Fast

questions.question: World population first reached one billion around:
The population explosion after 1800 was driven mainly by:
options: A sudden worldwide rise in birth rates
Mass migration to new continents
Collapsing death rates from better food, clean water, vaccines and antibiotics, while births stayed high
Warmer global temperatures

questions.question: Calling the population graph a J-curve means:
options: Population rises and falls in regular cycles
Population fell before it rose
Growth has been constant throughout history
A long, almost flat tail across the centuries, then an elbow and a near-vertical climb

questions.question: The growth rate peaked near 2% in the late 1960s and has fallen since, yet the total keeps rising because:
options: A falling but still positive rate means slower growth, not decline — and huge past cohorts are now parents
The rate figures are wrongly measured
Death rates are rising faster than birth rates
Migration adds people to the world total

subtopics.title: Measuring Growth — Natural Increase and Doubling Time

questions.question: A country records 34 births and 9 deaths per thousand people per year. Its natural increase is:
options: 43 per thousand, or 4,3% a year
9 per thousand, or 0,9% a year
34 per thousand, or 3,4% a year
25 per thousand, or 2,5% a year

questions.question: Using the rule of 70, a population growing at 2,5% a year doubles in about:
options: 28 years
70 years
25 years
140 years

questions.question: Population growth compounds like interest on savings because:
options: Governments add people at a fixed rate
Each year's newcomers become parents themselves, so increase generates further increase
Birth rates rise automatically every year
Death rates fall automatically every year

questions.question: Which matching of country to growth situation from the lesson is correct?
options: Italy growing near 3%; Angola shrinking; South Africa negative
Angola near zero; Italy at 2,5%; South Africa doubling every 20 years
Angola near 3% with a young population; Italy with negative natural increase; South Africa near 1% and easing
All three countries growing at the same rate

questions.question: A region is overpopulated when:
options: Its density exceeds 100 people per square kilometre
Its population exceeds the carrying capacity of its resources and technology
Its total population exceeds ten million
Most of its people live in cities

questions.question: Singapore, with over 8 000 people per square kilometre, is NOT overpopulated because:
options: Its population is actually very small
Its climate prevents overpopulation
Density figures do not apply to islands
A wealthy, high-technology trading economy imports what its land cannot grow and sustains a high standard of living

questions.question: The sparsely settled far south of Madagascar can still be overpopulated because:
options: Rainfall is so meagre and soils so exhausted that even few people outstrip what the land can renew
Its cities are too large
Its density is above the world average
Too many tourists visit the region

questions.question: Carrying capacity can be LOWERED by:
options: Irrigation schemes
Improved seed varieties
Soil erosion, salinisation and emptied aquifers
Fertiliser use

questions.question: The most powerful measure on record for lowering birth rates is:
options: Building larger hospitals
The education of girls and women
Raising taxes on large families
Banning migration

questions.question: Cutting infant mortality lowers birth rates because:
options: Clinics discourage parents from having children
Fewer children are born in hospitals
It makes contraception unnecessary
Parents stop holding extra children as insurance once child survival becomes the norm

questions.question: China's one-child policy (1979-2015) is treated as a cautionary case because it:
options: Left an ageing society, a shrinking workforce and a skewed sex ratio, and births barely respond now that policy has reversed
Failed to reduce the birth rate at all
Was never actually enforced
Caused the population to double

questions.question: Bangladesh and Botswana matter in this debate because they:
options: Enforced one-child policies of their own
Achieved steep fertility declines through voluntary means — schooling, clinics and family planning — without coercion
Have the world's fastest-growing populations
Prove that birth rates cannot be changed

subtopics.title: The Festival That Fills in the Final Week

questions.question: In the year-long festival picture of population history, the first billion people are inside:
options: By the end of January
By the middle of winter
Only by Christmas morning, after nearly the whole year
In the first week of the year

questions.question: The gates roar in the final week because:
options: People suddenly started having far more babies
Death lost its grip — food, clean water, vaccines and antibiotics collapsed death rates while births carried on
The festival ground was enlarged
Migration between continents increased

questions.question: The queue outside the festival shrinking every year represents:
options: Rising death rates worldwide
The end of migration
A growing world population total
The falling growth rate, as families everywhere get smaller

subtopics.title: Too Many for What? The Overloaded Taxi

questions.question: In the taxi picture, the licence disc rated for fifteen passengers represents:
options: The region's carrying capacity
The region's population density
The region's birth rate
The region's total population

questions.question: "Full is not the same as overloaded" means:
options: Every dense region is overpopulated
A dense place with strong resources can be comfortable while a sparse place with weak resources is overstretched
Empty regions can never be overpopulated
Density and overpopulation are identical measures

questions.question: A district can become overloaded without a single new person arriving when:
options: Its birth rate rises sharply
Its young people return from the cities
Drought, erosion or exhausted boreholes shrink the resource base beneath the same population
New clinics are built

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of overpopulation strain named in the lesson?
options: Falling school enrolment
Rising wages in every sector
Expanding forests
Plots divided until they cannot feed a family, bare grazed hillsides and shack settlements outrunning water pipes

questions.question: The chain from the school gate to the birth rate runs:
options: Girl completes school, marries later, earns and invests in fewer children, uses family planning — birth rate falls
Girl completes school, moves to a city, birth rate rises
School fees rise, families shrink to afford them
Schools teach smaller families as a law

questions.question: Helping more babies survive slows growth because:
options: Hospitals limit family size
Parents no longer keep spare children as insurance once survival becomes ordinary
Surviving children never have children of their own
It raises the death rate later

questions.question: Pensions help lower birth rates because:
options: Pensioners cannot raise children
They make large families more affordable
They are only paid to small families
Where the state supports the elderly, children stop being a retirement plan

questions.question: South Africa's fertility fell from about six children per woman to about 2,3 through:
options: A legal limit on family size
Compulsory family planning
Urbanisation, women's education, clinic-based family planning and safer infancy — by choice, not force
Mass emigration
